correctness.rationale: The actual RESULT.md proof splits the cyclic 2p transform via CRT Z_2 x Z_p into h_+=f_0+f_1 and h_-=f_0-f_1. With both channels nonzero, each has time support <=k, so Tao's prime-order uncertainty lower bound gives >=2(p-k+1) Fourier coefficients. A vanishing channel forces equal/opposite slices and even exact support k=2r, giving >=p-r+1. For each s<=p, the polynomial product_{j=0}^{s-2}(X-zeta^j) has s-1 distinct prime-root Fourier zeros and, by the same prime uncertainty bound, all its s coefficients nonzero. It realizes the two possible channel mechanisms with EXACT k, proving the two candidate bounds are sharp. Algebra gives crossover 3r=p+1 and the claimed p-7 jump. The proof is for complex arbitrary signals and k<=p only; no monotonicity of the exact-k invariant is assumed. The finite checker is corroboration, not the infinite proof.
